# Actual cap credit at one homothetic contact facet

This is a local, simultaneously realizable first-variation statement for
three actual fibers. It retains each ambient cap, rather than replacing
the endpoint costs by their unmarked normal masses. It does not infer a
global OC bound by integrating ratios which depend on the normal.

## 1. Geometric and deformation hypotheses

Let A,B be full-dimensional SIMPLE polytopes in R^d, d>=2, with the same
normal fan, and let K=(A+B)/2. Regard them as the three integer fibers
at bases -1,0,1. Their convex hull has precisely these integer fibers.
Fix a common facet unit normal u. Suppose its three exposed facets admit
one common parametrization

    a(x)=a_0+r_A x, b(x)=b_0+r_B x,
    m(x)=(a(x)+b(x))/2,             x in F,                (1)

where F is a (d-1)-dimensional convex body in u-perp and r_A,r_B>0.
Thus the endpoint facets are positively homothetic, not reflected.
Put k=d-1 and

    sigma_A=r_A^k |F|, sigma_B=r_B^k |F|,
    sigma_K=((r_A+r_B)/2)^k |F|,
    C=sigma_A sigma_B/(sigma_A+sigma_B),
    rho=2C/sigma_K.                                     (2)

Then 0<rho<=1: the harmonic mean 2C is at most the geometric mean of
sigma_A,sigma_B, which in turn is at most sigma_K by ordinary BM.

Fix h>0 and move only the u-support plane of A inward at speed

    v_A=2h sigma_B/(sigma_A+sigma_B),
    v_B=2h sigma_A/(sigma_A+sigma_B)                     (3)

for B. Write the resulting polytopes A_epsilon,B_epsilon, and set
K_epsilon=(A_epsilon+B_epsilon)/2. This is an ACTUAL compatible nested
three-fiber deformation for all sufficiently small epsilon>=0.

Here are the support details. For a simple polytope, sufficiently small
changes of its support numbers with the fixed facet normals preserve its
normal fan: each old vertex is the unique intersection of its d active
planes, and its finitely many inactive inequalities retain their strict
slack. Each candidate intersection for another d-subset which is not an
old vertex retains a violated inequality, unless its active normals are
dependent, in which case it does not define a vertex. Equivalently the
old simplicial normal cones remain the same complete fan. Apply this to
both endpoint polytopes. On that common fan support functions are linear
on each cone. Their average is the support function with averaged facet
support numbers. Thus K_epsilon has that same fan, its u-support moves
inward at speed (v_A+v_B)/2=h, and every other original facet support
number is unchanged. No unrecorded source-facet motion occurs.

## 2. The exact simultaneous cap inequality

For any closed ambient halfspace H in R times R^d let I_A,I_B,I_K be
its INWARD facet traces on the three exposed facets. For a proper
tangential cut this is the usual closed trace up to a surface-null set.
At an entire facet coincidence it is one if the inward side is captured,
zero otherwise. This is precisely the limit of the indicator at a facet
point moved a positive infinitesimal distance into the fiber; it handles
supporting cuts without assigning them their incorrect closed-face loss.
Pure-integer halfspaces are included and have their constant fiber bits.

The parametrization (1) and the ambient affine margin give

    L_K(m(x))=(L_A(a(x))+L_B(b(x)))/2.

Moreover (3) has v_A+v_B=2h. The same identity holds after displacing
a(x),b(x),m(x) inward by tau v_A u,tau v_B u,tau h u, respectively,
for every tau>0. Consequently, pointwise for almost every x in F,

    I_A(a(x))+I_B(b(x)) >= I_K(m(x)).                     (4)

This proof proves (4) for every cap in one finite or infinite menu using
the SAME pairing and the SAME deformation. It does not optimize a
different coupling for each cap. Define its normalized source trace

    q_H=(1/sigma_K) integral_(K(u)) I_K dH_k.

At a fixed facet, the lost volume from a cut is its inward speed times
the integral of its inward trace, to first order. This follows directly
by integrating parallel slices over the removed layer; the facet boundary
and a proper trace boundary are null. If a cap coincides with the facet,
the correct inward trace gives the exact one-sided sign. Thus, writing
Delta_H for the sum of captured volumes removed from ALL three fibers,
(2)--(4) give

    lim_(epsilon down 0) Delta_H/epsilon
      =h integral_(K(u)) I_K
          +v_A integral_(A(u)) I_A+v_B integral_(B(u)) I_B
      >=h(sigma_K+2C) q_H
      =h sigma_K(1+rho) q_H.                             (5)

Indeed v_A sigma_A=v_B sigma_B=2hC. All other facets have zero normal
velocity; lower-dimensional edges have no first-order volume term.
The total removed mixed volume has exact first derivative

    T=h sigma_K+v_A sigma_A+v_B sigma_B
      =h sigma_K(1+2rho).                                (6)

Combining (5)--(6), for EVERY ambient closed cap,

    captured-loss derivative / T
       >= [(1+rho)/(1+2rho)] q_H >= (2/3)q_H.             (7)

The same inequalities hold after multiplying any finite menu by
nonnegative response weights and summing. No cap regularity is required
for these one-sided, inward-trace derivatives.

For equal translated endpoint facets, rho=1, both speeds are h, and
(5)--(6) say exactly: the three-fiber cost is three times the source cost,
while each captured loss is at least twice the source captured loss.

## 3. The precise limitation on assembling normals

The coefficient rho in (2) usually depends on u. Summing (5) over a set
of facet normals gives the rigorously retained expression

    sum_u h_u sigma_(K,u)(1+rho_u) q_(H,u),

whereas total cost is

    sum_u h_u sigma_(K,u)(1+2rho_u).

An ordinary centroid or projective boundary theorem controls a specified
weighted integral of q_(H,u); it does not automatically control the new
weight (1+rho_u). A lower bound for a ratio separately at each normal is
therefore not, by itself, a lower bound for the globally summed ratio.
Also, arbitrary endpoint faces need not admit the full parametrization
(1); their Minkowski facet may have a genuine volume excess not covered
by one uniform midpoint coupling. The preceding theorem assumes neither
an unproved uniform facet identification nor an unproved global payment.

The common-fan simplicity hypothesis is only a sufficient realization
condition. The trace and algebraic parts (4)--(7) apply whenever the
indicated actual facet velocities and no additional first-order boundary
costs have been independently justified. This note does not remove that
realizability requirement.
